reference_sql:
SELECT product_id, product_name, unit_cost_eur
FROM products
WHERE unit_cost_eur > (SELECT AVG(unit_cost_eur) FROM products)
alternatives:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.unit_cost_eur
FROM products p
JOIN (
  -- one row in total
  SELECT AVG(unit_cost_eur) AS avg_cost_eur
  FROM products
) AS a ON p.unit_cost_eur > a.avg_cost_eur

WITH avg_cost AS (
  -- one row in total
  SELECT AVG(unit_cost_eur) AS avg_cost_eur
  FROM products
)
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.unit_cost_eur
FROM products p
CROSS JOIN avg_cost a
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur > a.avg_cost_eur

other_way.sql:
WITH avg_cost AS (
  -- one row in total
  SELECT AVG(unit_cost_eur) AS avg_cost_eur
  FROM products
)
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.unit_cost_eur
FROM products p
CROSS JOIN avg_cost a
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur > a.avg_cost_eur
other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step that holds the average, joined to every product, works too, but one value fits more plainly in WHERE.
